slot.brief: For a balanced gas-phase reaction (e.g. combustion), compute Δn_g and convert between ΔH and ΔU at temperature T.

stem: For $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightarrow2\text{NH}_3(g)$, $\Delta U=-100.0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ at $300\ \text{K}$. Find $\Delta H$. Take $R=8.0\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: For the reaction as written, Δn_g = 2 − 4 = −2. Thus ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT = −100.0 − 2(8.0)(300)/1000 = −104.8 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Delta n_g=2-(1+3)=-2$.
$\Delta H=\Delta U+\Delta n_gRT$.
$\Delta n_gRT=(-2)(8.0)(300)=-4800\ \text{J mol}^{-1}=-4.8\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
$\Delta H=-100.0-4.8=-104.8\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Independent check: For the reaction as written, Δn_g = 2 − 4 = −2. Thus ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT = −100.0 − 2(8.0)(300)/1000 = −104.8 kJ mol⁻¹.
solution:
For gaseous reactions, $\Delta H=\Delta U+\Delta n_gRT$, where $\Delta n_g=2-(1+3)=-2$.
$$\Delta H=-100.0+\frac{(-2)(8.0)(300)}{1000}=-104.8\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$
